display.purpose: Range headline, page titles, the detail panel's code and the report period; 1.75rem below 720px.

headline.purpose: Reading-page section heads in navy with a hairline beneath, and sheet titles.

title.purpose: An obligation's name under its code; ledes use the size at 400 and 1.5, block headings at 600.

body.purpose: Running text; prose capped at 70ch at a 1.6 line height.

body-sm.purpose: Tables, detail sections, notes and the footer.

figure.purpose: The figure voice: obligation codes in navy and headline counts, tabular figures.

control.purpose: Buttons, segmented options, masthead tabs, footer links and disclosure summaries.

label.purpose: Column heads, field labels, list headings, meta lines and pills; sentence case, never uppercase.

mono.purpose: Fragment Mono for code identifiers only, on a Tag Grey chip; never for numbers.

shadows.name: control-lift
shadows.purpose: Resting lift on buttons, inputs, selects and the file check; dropped by quiet and disabled buttons and in print.

shadows.name: segment-on
shadows.purpose: Current segment of the segmented control: the control lift plus a Hairline ring.

shadows.name: float
shadows.purpose: The timeline tooltip and the report sheet on screen.

shadows.name: sheet
shadows.purpose: Right-hand dialogs, over a rgba(16, 24, 40, 0.42) backdrop.

shadows.name: masthead-edge
shadows.purpose: A 1px edge under the sticky masthead; a rule, not depth.

shadows.name: input-focus-halo
shadows.purpose: Focus state of text inputs, with a Cobalt border; a state signal, not depth.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: The only easing: every transition and the sheet entrance.

motion.name: duration-control
motion.purpose: Color, border and shadow changes on buttons, inputs, chips, segmented options and tabs.

motion.name: duration-file-check
motion.purpose: Border, color and fill on the file check.

motion.name: duration-row
motion.purpose: Hover fill on table rows and calendar days.

motion.name: sheet-in
motion.purpose: The one entrance: right-hand dialogs slide in.

motion.name: skeleton
motion.purpose: Loading shimmer from Cool Panel Grey through Tag Grey.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: prefers-reduced-motion collapses every animation and transition.

breakpoints.name: split
breakpoints.purpose: max-width: the table and aside stack; the detail opens as a sheet.

breakpoints.name: masthead-wrap
breakpoints.purpose: max-width: tabs take their own row and scroll behind a right-edge fade.

breakpoints.name: phone
breakpoints.purpose: max-width: titles step down, rows stack, the month grid shows dots.

breakpoints.name: timeline-narrow
breakpoints.purpose: Chart container width: short lane names, smaller marks, two-digit years, no callout.

breakpoints.name: profile-compact
breakpoints.purpose: max-width: the profile button keeps only its icon.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The one cobalt action in a group: Mark filed, Print, Save profile, Subscribe to this obligation.

components.name: Secondary Button

components.name: Search Field
components.description: 38px field with a Control Rule border and the control lift; Hover Rule on hover; Cobalt border and a 16% Cobalt halo on focus.

India Compliance Calendar
OverviewCalendarPlannerReportUpdates

components.name: Horizon Segmented Control

components.name: Status Pills and Law Tag

narrative.overview:
The compliance year is typeset the way a listed company sets its annual report. A deep navy masthead sits over white working pages, and the content below it is ruled tables with tabular figures, short lists under section rules, and a single chart that shows how the horizon's deadlines fall law by law. The register is corporate and clean: a document the board would accept, read at a desk and equally at home on a phone between meetings. Density is high but calm. One working page carries a headline, a row of controls, a full-width chart and a long table without crowding, because separation comes from hairlines, tonal bands and generous section spacing rather than from boxes.

Color is held back so that it can carry meaning. Navy is the ink of record: the masthead, every obligation code, the headline figures, the rule that opens each section, and every ordinary due date on the chart. A single cobalt marks what can be acted on or what is selected. Four muted state hues (overdue red, due-soon amber, extension blue, filed green) appear only where the state itself is the message. Type is one family, Archivo at its normal width, separated into roles by weight: semibold headings, a heavier figure voice for codes and figures, regular prose. Depth is nearly absent; surfaces are flat and tonal, and shadow only lifts a control by a hair or floats a transient layer.

The system replaces a dark catalog look the user tried and rejected, and it refuses the pastel SaaS dashboard of count tiles. The product's confirmed rejections carry into the visual system: no alarm red everywhere, no walls of legal text, nothing playful or gamified.
keyCharacteristics: Navy masthead over white working pages and cool grey panels; light only.
Ruled tables with tabular figures; hairlines, not boxes, separate content.
A 2px navy rule opens every working section.
One cobalt for action and selection; state hues only where state is the message.
One family (Archivo, normal width) with a 650 figure voice for codes and figures.
One chart: the swimlane timeline, its marks sized by the cost of filing late.
Flat surfaces; shadow only for control lift, floating layers and dialogs.

rules.name: The One Cobalt Rule
rules.body: Cobalt is the only hue that means act or selected: primary buttons, links, toggled filters, the selected row, day and range, focus, and Today on the chart. Nothing decorative is cobalt. Two places mark selection differently, and both are deliberate: the segmented control shows its current value as a raised white segment with navy text, and on navy the current tab uses the lighter #8fb0ff bar.

rules.name: The State Is the Message Rule
rules.body: Red, amber, extension blue and green appear only on an element whose message is that state: status pills, timeline marks and the status-count dots that serve as their legend, calendar code chips, the file check, the extension note, and status cells and figures in the report. Never as a section color, heading color, row stripe or page wash.

rules.name: The Quiet Red Rule
rules.body: Red means overdue and nothing else. The Overdue count turns red only when it is above zero, and so does the report's Overdue figure; with nothing overdue, the only red left on screen is the legend dot of the Overdue filter.

rules.name: The Figure Voice Rule
rules.body: Codes, counts and headline figures take the figure voice (650, -0.015em, tabular); dates and amounts in tables take 600 with tabular figures, and every table is tabular by default. Obligation codes are navy unless a state chip recolors them or a filed row fades them.

rules.name: The Sentence-Case Label Rule
rules.body: Labels are 12px semibold at +0.01em, in sentence case, in Caption Slate (Slate Ink for field labels). No uppercase, no wide tracking, no small caps.

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: Archivo at normal width carries every role from the 3rem entry code to the 9.5px chart counts. Do not reach for its condensed or expanded widths or add a second display face, and do not set numbers in Fragment Mono.

rules.name: The Ruled Section Rule
rules.body: A working section opens with a 2px navy rule across its full width (the chart, each aside list, the detail panel, the calendar's day list, the report's key figures), and its rows are divided by 1px Hairline Rules. Boxes are the exception, never the container.

rules.name: The Paper Flat Rule
rules.body: Content does not float. Tables, lists, panels and the chart lie flat on the page; only controls (by a hair), the tooltip, the on-screen report sheet and dialogs carry shadow.

rules.name: The Round Ends Rule
rules.body: Full pills belong to statuses and law filters. Buttons that do something (file, print, export, subscribe, save) are 6px rectangles.

rules.name: The One Chart Rule
rules.body: The swimlane timeline is the system's only chart. Other surfaces show the same data as ruled tables, the month grid and lists; no sparklines, rings or secondary charts.

dos: Do open every working section with the 2px navy rule and divide its rows with 1px Hairline Rules (#e2e7ee).
Do keep Cobalt (#1d4ed8) for the primary action, links, toggled filters, selection, focus and Today, with at most one primary button per action group.
Do set codes, counts and headline figures in the figure voice (650, -0.015em, tabular figures), and keep codes navy.
Do show state with a pill or a mark in the state's color, and use the state's text tone (overdue-text, soon-text, extended-text, filed-text) for any state-colored text.
Do leave an ordinary upcoming item navy and pill-less in tables and lists; color is for exceptions.
Do put legal text, penalty bases and change notes behind a disclosure, and show every rule's sources with its verified date.
Do draw icons from the Lucide set at 16px with a 1.75 stroke, round caps and joins, in the current text color; the calendar-check mark is the product's own.
Do theme the browser's own surfaces from the palette: #d6e2ff selection, a thin #c3cbd6 scrollbar, a Cobalt caret, 1px Cobalt Line underlines offset 0.2em, and Cobalt checkboxes and sliders.
Do move state changes on the system ease-out (cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)) at 120 to 150ms, keep the sheet's 220ms slide as the one entrance, and honor reduced motion.
donts: Don't bring back a dark ground or the dark catalog look this system replaced; it is light only.
Don't build count tiles or hero metrics on working surfaces; counts are compact filter buttons, and the large-figure strip belongs to the printable report.
Don't use red for anything but overdue, and don't color a count red at zero.
Don't add a second accent hue, or use a state hue as decoration, a section color, a row stripe or a page wash.
Don't make cards the page structure or nest boxes; working content lives in ruled sections and hairline rows, and bordered panels stay limited to the cases under Cards / Containers.
Don't add a second chart, sparklines or progress rings.
Don't uppercase or letter-space labels, and don't set numbers in Fragment Mono; it is for code identifiers only.
Don't use Archivo's condensed or expanded widths, or a second display face.
Don't lift content with shadow; only controls, the tooltip, the on-screen report sheet and dialogs carry it.
Don't add gradient fills, gradient text, glass or blur; the only gradients in the system are functional (the select caret, the loading shimmer, the masthead's scroll fade).
Don't add playful or gamified touches such as illustrations, emoji or celebrations on filing; a filed item simply turns green and goes quiet.
Don't set white text on the amber due-soon solid; amber carries text only as soon-text on its tint.
